exercises.prompt: In the passive past سُئِلَ ('he was asked'), why is the medial hamza written on ئـ?
choices: Because kasrah on the hamza is stronger than the preceding ḍammah
Because ḍammah is stronger than kasrah
Because hamza always sits on ئـ in passive verbs
exercises.answer: Because kasrah on the hamza is stronger than the preceding ḍammah
exercises.explanation: The vowel-strength hierarchy is kasrah > ḍammah > fatḥah > sukūn; kasrah wins and requires seat ئـ.

exercises.prompt: Select the correct seat for final hamza after a long vowel in جَاءَ ('he came'):
exercises.explanation: Final hamza preceded by a long vowel or sukūn is written on the line (ء).

feedback.rule: Final hamza after long vowel/sukūn sits on the line.
